response.sql:
SELECT p.ID, p.SEX, AVG(l.ALP) AS avg_alp, AVG(l.HCT) AS avg_hct
FROM Patient p
JOIN Laboratory l ON l.ID = p.ID
WHERE p.ID IN (
    SELECT ID FROM Laboratory
    WHERE `U-PRO` = '-' AND RA = '-'
)
GROUP BY p.ID, p.SEX
ORDER BY avg_hct IS NULL, avg_hct DESC
LIMIT 10;

assumptions.assumption: A patient qualifies if at least one lab record has both U-PRO = '-' and RA = '-' on the same record (same test date). The request does not say whether the two tests must come from the same visit.
'-' is the literal stored value for a negative result, and the averages are taken over all of the patient's Laboratory rows, with NULLs ignored by AVG and no rounding.
Only patients with a row in Patient are returned (inner join), and SEX is used as stored. Ties in average HCT are ordered arbitrarily.

alternatives.interpretation: The U-PRO '-' result and the RA '-' result may come from different lab records, so a patient qualifies if they have any record with U-PRO '-' and any record (possibly another date) with RA '-'.
